- If sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for mean reversion or short-term rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above prior peak for next 3–5 periods.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive days below 70), model tends to lag; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% per lagged day.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often fails to capture sentiment shifts; align forecast slope with sentiment transition points (e.g., if sentiment flips from 0.67→0.00, reduce forecast slope).
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits recent trends; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 5-day moving average) to forecast to reduce volatility bias.
